SAVED ACCESS PLAN

Changing this label does not remove existing VPN profiles. Record router removals in the device checklist below.

1

Set up each remote device

One router profile per device. The same person’s phone and laptop need separate profiles.

VPN access and library permissions are separate. This router’s VPN can provide home-network access; a User role limits the library, not other home services. Client routing settings are not a substitute for router access controls.
Show the router setup procedure
  1. Open the TP-Link router, then Advanced → VPN Server → WireGuard.
  2. Keep the existing server enabled, port 51820, and Home Network Only.
  3. Click Add. Give the profile a unique name such as Alex-Phone. Keep the new address assigned by the router; do not reuse another device’s address.
  4. For a library-only route, set Allowed IPs (Client) to 192.168.1.64/32. Leave Allowed IPs (Server) at that device’s assigned address. This controls routing, not enforced network isolation.
  5. Save and export the profile or show its QR code directly to the intended device. In the device’s WireGuard app, use peer endpoint vpn.discerntechnologies.com:51820. Leave its keys and assigned address unchanged.
  6. Deliver that configuration privately. Do not upload its private key, configuration file or QR code to this page. Record only the profile name and address below.

The router supports up to 16 profiles. The public-IP updater is already maintained separately on MAHA.

Device checklists are your records. MAHA does not create, inspect, verify or delete router profiles automatically.

2

Prepare their HTTPS certificate

Each new desktop or phone must trust the MAHA public certificate once before opening the secure library. Send this public certificate alongside the setup instructions.

Download public MAHA certificate
Show certificate installation steps
  • Windows: import MAHA-Local-Root-CA.crt into the current user’s Trusted Root Certification Authorities store. Restart the browser if required.
  • Android: Settings → Security / More security settings → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate. Select the downloaded file. Names vary by phone.
  • iPhone/iPad: open the certificate, install the downloaded profile in Settings, then enable trust under General → About → Certificate Trust Settings.

This device will trust certificates issued by your MAHA certificate authority. Share only the public certificate, never its private key. Don’t bypass certificate warnings.

3

Create their library invitation

Email invitation & instructions

The email button opens your email app; send the prepared message there and attach the public certificate. Deliver VPN credentials privately. The invitation expires in 7 days and works once. Links are shown only when created; renewing invalidates the previous link.

Account changes revoke existing library sessions. The last active Super user cannot be disabled or demoted.

4

Verify it together

  1. Have them trust the certificate and accept the invitation to create their own password.
  2. For a remote test, turn Wi-Fi off on the phone and enable its WireGuard tunnel.
  3. Open https://192.168.1.64/, sign in, and open a book without a certificate warning.
  4. For a User account, check that uploading and account management are unavailable. Record the completed test in that device’s checklist.

For a local-only user, test on the home network without WireGuard.

Remove access later

Disable library access here to cancel outstanding invitations and sign out that person’s sessions immediately. Then remove each of their VPN profiles from the router and record those removals above.

This button does not disable the router profiles. Until you remove them on the router, their VPN network access can remain available.
